summary
Summary
Participants chose between working alone for a sure profit and working together for a slightly higher profit that is earned only if the partner(s) also choose to work together. What each participant was told about the partner's knowledge of the payoff (primary, secondary, tertiary or common knowledge) and the payoff size were manipulated. Reported: coordination attempts were higher with common knowledge than with tertiary (shared) knowledge in every payoff condition of all three experiments.

instructions
Instruction content (paraphrase of the paper's description)
Participants read that they would earn a minimum of 50 cents, which they could augment based on their decisions in their interaction with another participant on Mechanical Turk. One of them would play a butcher and the other a baker. Each could either work alone for a sure profit (the butcher could make chicken wings, the baker dinner rolls) or attempt to work with their partner, the butcher making hot dogs, the baker the buns. By choosing to work together the participant can earn a profit, but only if the partner also chooses to work together; if either decides to collaborate but the partner does not, that person doesn't earn anything, because they cannot sell a bun without a hot dog or vice versa. They would earn a certain amount ($1, $2, $5, or $10) if they decided to work alone, but the hot dog price varied from day to day, and thus the earnings for working together might be more than or less than this sure profit. The information about hot dog earnings might be conveyed by a messenger boy (displayed on their screen in a private box that only they could see), or by a loudspeaker (displayed in a public box that the other participant could see on his or her screen as well).

Instruction content (paraphrase of the paper's description)
Participants read that they would earn a minimum of 50 cents, which they could augment based on their decisions in their interaction with another participant on Mechanical Turk. One of them would play a butcher and the other a baker. Each could either work alone for a sure profit (the butcher could make chicken wings, the baker dinner rolls) or attempt to work with their partner, the butcher making hot dogs, the baker the buns. By choosing to work together the participant can earn a profit, but only if the partner also chooses to work together; if either decides to collaborate but the partner does not, that person doesn't earn anything, because they cannot sell a bun without a hot dog or vice versa. They would earn a certain amount ($1, $2, $5, or $10) if they decided to work alone, but the hot dog price varied from day to day, and thus the earnings for working together might be more than or less than this sure profit. The information about hot dog earnings might be conveyed by a messenger boy (displayed on their screen in a private box that only they could see), or by a loudspeaker (displayed in a public box that the other participant could see on his or her screen as well).

issues.title: Data and materials availability not stated
issues.reason: The manuscript text does not state whether data or the full materials are shared.
issues.impact: Cannot verify reported cell percentages or reproduce unstated instrument wording from the paper alone.
issues.suggestedAction: Ask the authors or the researcher for the data and full instruments.

issues.title: Assignment of participants to cells and roles not described
issues.reason: The paper says knowledge state and payoff were varied between subjects with 100 recruited per condition, but not how participants were assigned.
issues.impact: The replay assigns arms equally; real assignment could differ.
issues.suggestedAction: Confirm random, equal assignment to the 16 cells and to butcher/baker, or supply the mechanism.

issues.title: Blinding not reported
issues.reason: Not stated.
issues.suggestedAction: None needed unless the authors report otherwise.

issues.title: Number completing not reported
issues.reason: Only recruited (1600) and analysed (1033) are given.
issues.impact: Exclusion rate cannot be separated from non-completion.

issues.title: Exclusion criterion for comprehension failures
issues.reason: The paper excludes participants with incorrect answers to the payoff comprehension questions but does not say whether any single error excluded them.
issues.impact: The replay's exclusion rule is an implementation assumption (any incorrect payoff answer).
issues.suggestedAction: Confirm the criterion with the authors.

issues.title: Placeholder values in the common knowledge message
issues.reason: The printed message contains [today's price] and [earnings for working together]; the relation between the two amounts is not stated.
issues.impact: The replay must fill in both values.
issues.suggestedAction: Decide the values (e.g. both set to the together-payoff). Recorded as a replay adaptation.

issues.title: Butcher-perspective wording not printed
issues.reason: Messages are given from the baker's perspective only.
issues.suggestedAction: Researcher to approve a role swap (Butcher<->Baker, bakery<->butcher shop) or supply the original.

issues.title: Instruction wording not printed
issues.reason: Instructions are described in prose, not printed. A supplied replication survey (Exeter, GBP) prints similar wording but is a different instrument.
issues.impact: The replay presents the reported content in second person, not original wording.
issues.suggestedAction: Supply the original instruction text or approve the reported-content version.

issues.title: Instructions are a paraphrase
issues.reason: Field is labelled reported because the wording is not printed.
issues.impact: Participants' reading of the task may differ from the original.
issues.suggestedAction: Review the paraphrase against the original materials.

issues.title: Payoff reveal wording in primary/secondary/tertiary not printed
issues.reason: Only the common knowledge message prints the amount.
issues.impact: How the potential profit is shown in other conditions is unspecified.
issues.suggestedAction: State the amount in the reveal (ten cents more than the sure profit); record as an adaptation.

issues.title: Silent loudspeaker wording
issues.reason: The public box 'stated that the loudspeaker was silent'; exact wording not given.
issues.suggestedAction: Supply the original wording if available.

issues.title: Decision prompt not printed
issues.reason: Prompt and option labels are not printed in the paper.

issues.title: Full comprehension sets not printed

issues.suggestedAction: Approve survey wording or supply the original.

issues.title: Demographic items not printed

issues.title: Expected earnings formula as printed
